## What it is

Metabase connects to your databases and lets you ask questions of the data, with or without SQL, then turn the answers into charts and dashboards ([metabase/metabase](https://github.com/metabase/metabase)).

**Licence:** `AGPL-3.0`. The repository mixes the AGPL with the Metabase Commercial License (the `enterprise/` directory), and `LICENSE.txt` at v0.65.3 says the binaries "located at hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase ... are released under the AGPL". This package uses that image, not `metabase-enterprise`. GitHub reports `NOASSERTION`, so the licence gate relies on the license-matrix row "Metabase". Market class **L2**.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): monitoring: analytics, dashboards. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with Metabase (Java) and PostgreSQL 18 as its application database, a native sidecar on 127.0.0.1 only. PostgreSQL trusts local connections, so there is no database password and no Secret.
- `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is generated once by an init container and kept on the database volume; it encrypts the connection details of the databases you add. Lose the volume and both go together, which is the point: a backup of one is a backup of the other.
- Non-root: Metabase as UID 2000 (the UID upstream's script would switch to), PostgreSQL as UID 70 (the Alpine image's `postgres` user). No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- `MB_ANON_TRACKING_ENABLED=false`: no anonymous usage statistics.
- Volume: `metabase-db` (5 GiB).
- Probes: `GET /api/health`; startup allows 15 minutes for the first migrations.

## First run

Source: [Metabase docs, Running Metabase on Docker](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/installation-and-operation/running-metabase-on-docker).

1. Install Metabase from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-metabase`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:3000:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-metabase port-forward svc/metabase 3000:3000
   ```
3. The setup page creates the admin account. Do it right after install: whoever reaches it first becomes the admin.
4. Add a database to query. Other apps' databases on this box listen on 127.0.0.1 inside their own pods and are not reachable; connect to databases that accept network connections.

## Not done yet

- No email (SMTP): invitations and alerts are not mailed.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: Metabase writes its plugins to `/plugins` in the image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none for containers. Idle memory was measured on a k3s smoke test (arm64, 2026-11-12) and the figures were raised to leave headroom above it. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (metabase)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/postgres:18.6-trixie`: CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6, fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7 or 1.26.0-rc.3.
- Secret finding (Trivy): the same postgres image has `private-key` (HIGH) in `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key` (Debian's ssl-cert package).
- Passed: the metabase v0.65.3 image, licence (matrix row matches), ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.

**Unblock attempt (apps/market-unblock-2, 2026-11-13):** Only the bundled `postgres:18.6-trixie` blocked this app (the Metabase `v0.65.3` image, licence, ClamAV and smoke test passed). The sidecar moved to `postgres:18.6-alpine`, the same image `paperless-ngx` uses (tag and digest read from the Docker Hub registry on 2026-11-13; digest `sha256:9ba53c7d…193085b`). The Alpine image uses `su-exec` (C) instead of the Go helper `gosu` and has no Debian `ssl-cert` package, which is where CVE-2025-68121 and the snakeoil private key came from. It has not been scanned by us yet: the CI gate decides the tier, and this app stays `blocked` until a run passes. The Alpine `postgres` user is UID/GID 70 (Debian: 999). Alpine uses musl, so text sorting differs from the Debian image; a database made by one image must not be opened by the other, which is safe only because nobody has installed this app yet. Metabase `v0.65.4` exists but is not needed for this fix.
